personas.name: Duplicate dose refused, then overridden with a reason
personas.description: Eleanor took her 8 a.m. pills at 8:05. At 10:30 she says she took her blood-pressure pill again. The dose guard must refuse the duplicate, and record it only after an explicit "record it anyway" that comes with a reason — which also raises a dose_override alert for Priya.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I took my blood pressure pill, the lisinopril

replyIncludes: You already took Lisinopril at 8:05 a.m. today

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: Yes, record it anyway because Dr. Chen told me to double it today.

personas.name: Override confirmed without a reason is still refused
personas.description: Same duplicate as above, but Eleanor confirms without saying why. Confirmation alone must not record the dose: the guard asks for the reason first, and records only once one is given. (The rule brain forwards a reason only when a "because/since" clause exists; Bedrock may instead ask why without calling the tool — either way nothing may be recorded.)

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I took my lisinopril

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: Yes, record it anyway.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: Record it anyway because the doctor said to double it today.

personas.name: An ambiguous name gets a clarifying question, not a guess
personas.description: Two of Eleanor's medications are for blood pressure. "My blood pressure pill" must not be resolved by guessing: the tool lists the candidates and the assistant asks which one. Once she names it, the duplicate guard applies to the clarified medication.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I took my blood pressure pill

replyIncludes: Do you mean Lisinopril or Amlodipine?

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I took the amlodipine

replyIncludes: You already took Amlodipine at 8:05 a.m. today

personas.name: A brand name resolves to the generic and the dose is allowed
personas.description: Eleanor calls her Warfarin by its brand name. Coumadin must resolve to Warfarin, and since the evening Warfarin has not been taken yet (and yesterday's was over 12 hours ago) the guard allows it with no alert.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I just had my Coumadin

personas.name: A second Metformin 30 minutes after the first is refused (minimum interval)
personas.description: Metformin is allowed twice a day, so the daily maximum is not the problem — the 4-hour minimum interval is. At 8:35, thirty minutes after the 8:05 dose, a second Metformin must be refused, and the plan afterwards must still show only the three morning doses taken. (Against a live server the demo reset keeps the real clock's seconds, so the guard may say 31 minutes; the check only pins the interval wording.)

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I took my metformin

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: What's my plan today?

replyIncludes: Next up is Metformin at 6 p.m.

personas.name: A watch-level symptom is noted for the dashboard without paging anyone
personas.description: "Tired" is on the watch list: the check-in is flagged and an informational alert lands on the dashboard for Priya to see, but nobody is notified and there is no emergency wording.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I'm just tired today

replyIncludes: noted it for Priya Whitfield-Singh to see

personas.name: An urgent symptom pages the priority-1 caregiver without emergency guidance
personas.description: Dizziness is urgent for someone on blood-pressure medication and a blood thinner: a critical alert notifies Priya (priority 1) only, the reply suggests a call, and there is no emergency guidance and no mention of Daniel.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I'm feeling a bit dizzy this morning

personas.name: An emergency phrase gets the guidance first and alerts both caregivers
personas.description: Trouble breathing is an emergency phrase. Whether it goes through the check-in (rule brain) or call_for_help (Bedrock is told to use it for breathing trouble), the emergency guidance must open the reply verbatim and both caregivers must be notified.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I feel like I can't breathe

replyIncludes: This could be an emergency. Please call 911 right now.

personas.name: "Help, I fell" calls for help: guidance first, everyone alerted
personas.description: A fall reported with "help" must go straight to call_for_help: a critical help alert notifies every caregiver and the reply opens with the emergency guidance.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: Help, I fell in the kitchen

replyIncludes: This could be an emergency. Please call 911 right now.

personas.name: A caregiver hears the weekly summary, then adds ibuprofen and gets the interaction warnings
personas.description: Priya asks how her mother is doing (caregiver_summary), then adds ibuprofen for knee pain. add_medication is a caregiver tool the rule brain does not route, so the add goes through its REST twin, POST /api/dashboard/medications. The medication is added, but with two informational interaction warnings — Warfarin (major) first, Lisinopril (moderate) — the disclaimer, and an interaction alert that notifies Priya.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.utterance: How is Mom doing this week?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.utterance: Add ibuprofen 200 mg at 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. for knee pain

personas.name: Skipping a critical dose alerts the priority-1 caregiver
personas.description: At 7:30 p.m. (scenario "default": the morning doses are taken, the 6 p.m. ones are still open inside their grace window) Eleanor decides to skip tonight's Warfarin. Warfarin is critical, so the skip is recorded with her reason and a warning alert notifies Priya.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I'm going to skip my warfarin tonight because my stomach is upset

replyIncludes: marked your 6 p.m. Warfarin as skipped

personas.name: The plan asks for a check-in until one is recorded
personas.description: In the evening scenario five of six doses are taken and there has been no check-in today, so the plan ends with "How are you feeling today?". After a check-in with no symptoms (no alert, nobody notified) the same question no longer shows up in the plan.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: What's my plan tonight?

replyIncludes: Next up is Simvastatin at 9 p.m.

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: I'm feeling good tonight

turns.speaker: elder
turns.utterance: What's my plan tonight?

replyIncludes: Next up is Simvastatin at 9 p.m.
